text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Jospin conditions his backing of euro to the fight against unemployment
- Military court trial behind closed doors for (Colonel Juan Alberto).
- IU proposes maximum sanctions against Nueva Izquierda deputies.
- Truckers block European borders, asking for common labour laws.
EL MUNDO
- France questions sacrifices demanded by euro and shakes bourses.
- Defense Ministry orders Perote trial to take place behind closed doors to hide Cesid's "dirty linen"
- (Ex civil guard director) Roldan assures (former PM) Gonzalez gave his approval to illicit payments
DIARIO 16
- A couple of rascals:
(former colonel) Perote:.. Psoe wanted to buy me off with a golden retirement.
(former Civil guard director) Roldan:.. Gonzalez approved illicit payments.
- France to deflate euro balloon
- AIDS, the testimony of a doctor who is positive.
ABC
- Franch socialist government make the way toward EMU more difficult
CINCO DIAS
- Jospin asks for a break...and bourses fall
- The court judging (former financier) Conde to meet today to decide the day of the trial.
- Mannesman drops out of Retevision privatisation
- Spanish Bankinter to issue 10 trillion pesetas in subordinated bonds
- Audit firm Arthur Andersen doubts Cofir could cash receipts from the sale of its Portuguese holding Cofipsa.
EXPANSION
- France doubts over EMU drag markets down.
- Endesa imposes itself over Spanish BCH in the Retevision process
- Green light to the use of derivatives by investment trusts
- Dairy firms such as Danone, Nestle and Pascual to appeal against a 1.2 billion pesetas fine
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Spanish bank BBV starts a gradual exit from Endesa, of which it had up to a 1.1 percent.
- Mannesmann leaves Endesa and BCH standing alone in the fight for Retevision
- France's doubts over Stability Pact adds uncertainty to markets pessimism
